messages:
maya: Quick FYI — cost dashboard flagged ~18% of our GPU capacity idle but allocated across nodes this morning. Looks like lots of tiny leftover capacity on g4dn-style nodes that autoscaler won't reclaim because pods have nodeSelectors/labels.
sam: ugh. any examples?
maya: e.g. several batch-worker pods with `nodeSelector: gpu-type: a100-small` that only request 1 GPU on a node with 8 GPUs, they never get packed so 7 GPUs sit reserved.
linh: can you paste `kubectl get pods -o wide` for one of those namespaces?
maya: sure — snippet below:
```
NAMESPACE   NAME                     READY   STATUS    NODE                  GPU_REQUEST
batch-prod  batch-worker-58f4       1/1     Running   ip-10-0-2-45         1/8
batch-prod  batch-worker-9a2b       1/1     Running   ip-10-0-2-45         1/8
batch-prod  batch-worker-c3d7       1/1     Running   ip-10-0-2-45         1/8
```
maya: node label is `gpu-profile=a100-8` and each pod uses that selector. we end up with 5 nodes half full but no binpacking.
ops-bot: Alert: GPU waste >15% for cluster eu-west-1 (investigate) :warning:
ravi: two quick levers: 1) update sched policy to prefer packing (binpack) for that namespace, 2) enable descheduler to evict low-priority fragmented pods during off-peak.
sam: packing sounds good but we need to be careful — some long-running jobs pin to that label because of driver compat. migrating could cause restarts.
linh: can we use topologySpreadConstraint or podAffinity to keep same-tenant pods together instead of nodeSelector? might reduce cross-node spread without changing label usage.
maya: good call. also thinking of a migration plan: add toleration+taint on dedicated nodes for legacy drivers, then gradually retag new nodes without the taint and schedule new pods there. old pods can be drained/completed.
ravi: also consider lowering the default `requests.gpu` for some frameworks when using multi-instance GPU sharing (MIG) — saves a lot if model footprints allow.
sam: operationally, what about cluster-autoscaler? it's not scaling down because pods are 'unschedulable elsewhere' due to nodeSelector. we could add a descheduler hook after scale-up to try to consolidate.
linh: descheduler + CA scale-down together helped us before, but need eviction thresholds and pod priority settings so critical services don't bounce.
maya: action items: 1) I'll run a quick audit to list all pods with gpu nodeSelectors in the next hour (`kubectl get pods -A -o jsonpath=...`). 2) Ravi, can you draft a packing scheduler-policy? 3) Sam/Linh, own a migration plan for legacy-labels + taint.
ravi: will do, can ship a proposal by EOD.
ops-bot: Note: created ticket INFRA-4521 for "GPU packing + migration plan" and linked this thread.
sam: thanks — also please run cost projection after we simulate 25% improved packing, worth a follow-up with finance. :chart_with_upwards_trend: 
maya: sounds good. tagging @oncall if any of the planned evictions trigger alerts later.
linh: small follow-up — check node-affinity on StatefulSets, those are easy to miss.
maya: noted. I'll include that in the audit.
ops-bot: Reminder: descheduler job scheduled at 02:00 UTC daily; will skip namespaces labeled `no-deschedule=true`.
